- [QSelf](https://docs.rs/struct.QSelf.html)- `derive`or- `full`
- The explicit Self type in a qualified path: the `T`in`<T as Display>::fmt`.
- [Receiver](https://docs.rs/struct.Receiver.html)- `full`
- The `self`argument of an associated method.
- [Signature](https://docs.rs/struct.Signature.html)- `full`
- A function signature in a trait or implementation: `unsafe fn initialize(&self)`.
- [Stmt](https://docs.rs/struct.StmtMacro.html)- Macro - `full`
- A macro invocation in statement position.
- [Trait](https://docs.rs/struct.TraitBound.html)- Bound - `derive`or- `full`
- A trait used as a bound on a type parameter.
- [Trait](https://docs.rs/struct.TraitItemConst.html)- Item - Const - `full`
- An associated constant within the definition of a trait.
- [Trait](https://docs.rs/struct.TraitItemFn.html)- Item - Fn - `full`
- An associated function within the definition of a trait.
- [Trait](https://docs.rs/struct.TraitItemMacro.html)- Item - Macro - `full`
- A macro invocation within the definition of a trait.
- [Trait](https://docs.rs/struct.TraitItemType.html)- Item - Type - `full`
- An associated type within the definition of a trait.
- [Turbofish](https://docs.rs/struct.Turbofish.html)- `printing`and (- `derive`or- `full`)
- Returned by `TypeGenerics::as_turbofish`.
- [Type](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeArray.html)- Array - `derive`or- `full`
- A fixed size array type: `[T; n]`.
- [Type](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeBareFn.html)- Bare - Fn - `derive`or- `full`
- A bare function type: `fn(usize) -> bool`.
- [Type](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeGenerics.html)- Generics - `printing`and (- `derive`or- `full`)
- Returned by `Generics::split_for_impl`.
- [Type](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeGroup.html)- Group - `derive`or- `full`
- A type contained within invisible delimiters.
- [Type](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeImplTrait.html)- Impl - Trait - `derive`or- `full`
- An `impl Bound1 + Bound2 + Bound3`type where`Bound`is a trait or a lifetime.
- [Type](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeInfer.html)- Infer - `derive`or- `full`
- Indication that a type should be inferred by the compiler: `_`.
- [Type](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeMacro.html)- Macro - `derive`or- `full`
- A macro in the type position.
- [Type](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeNever.html)- Never - `derive`or- `full`
- The never type: `!`.
- [Type](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeParam.html)- Param - `derive`or- `full`
- A generic type parameter: `T: Into<String>`.
- [Type](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeParen.html)- Paren - `derive`or- `full`
- A parenthesized type equivalent to the inner type.
- [Type](https://docs.rs/struct.TypePath.html)- Path - `derive`or- `full`
- A path like `core::slice::Iter`, optionally qualified with a self-type as in`<Vec<T> as SomeTrait>::Associated`.
- [TypePtr](https://docs.rs/struct.TypePtr.html)- `derive`or- `full`
- A raw pointer type: `*const T`or`*mut T`.
- [Type](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeReference.html)- Reference - `derive`or- `full`
- A reference type: `&'a T`or`&'a mut T`.
- [Type](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeSlice.html)- Slice - `derive`or- `full`
- A dynamically sized slice type: `[T]`.
- [Type](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeTraitObject.html)- Trait - Object - `derive`or- `full`
- A trait object type `dyn Bound1 + Bound2 + Bound3`where`Bound`is a trait or a lifetime.
- [Type](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeTuple.html)- Tuple - `derive`or- `full`
- A tuple type: `(A, B, C, String)`.
- [UseGlob](https://docs.rs/struct.UseGlob.html)- `full`
- A glob import in a `use`item:`*`.
- [UseGroup](https://docs.rs/struct.UseGroup.html)- `full`
- A braced group of imports in a `use`item:`{A, B, C}`.
- [UseName](https://docs.rs/struct.UseName.html)- `full`
- An identifier imported by a `use`item:`HashMap`.
- [UsePath](https://docs.rs/struct.UsePath.html)- `full`
- A path prefix of imports in a `use`item:`core::...`.
- [UseRename](https://docs.rs/struct.UseRename.html)- `full`
- An renamed identifier imported by a `use`item:`HashMap as Map`.
- [Variadic](https://docs.rs/struct.Variadic.html)- `full`
- The variadic argument of a foreign function.
- [Variant](https://docs.rs/struct.Variant.html)- `derive`or- `full`
- An enum variant.
- [VisRestricted](https://docs.rs/struct.VisRestricted.html)- `derive`or- `full`
- A visibility level restricted to some path: `pub(self)`or`pub(super)`or`pub(crate)`or`pub(in some::module)`.
- [Where](https://docs.rs/struct.WhereClause.html)- Clause - `derive`or- `full`
- A `where`clause in a definition:`where T: Deserialize<'de>, D: 'static`.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Attr](https://docs.rs/enum.AttrStyle.html)- Style - `derive`or- `full`
- Distinguishes between attributes that decorate an item and attributes that are contained within an item.
- [BinOp](https://docs.rs/enum.BinOp.html)- `derive`or- `full`
- A binary operator: `+`,`+=`,`&`.
- [Captured](https://docs.rs/enum.CapturedParam.html)- Param - `full`
- Single parameter in a precise capturing bound.
- [Data](https://docs.rs/enum.Data.html)- `derive`
- The storage of a struct, enum or union data structure.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/enum.Expr.html)- `derive`or- `full`
- A Rust expression.
- [Field](https://docs.rs/enum.FieldMutability.html)- Mutability - `derive`or- `full`
- Unused, but reserved for RFC 3323 restrictions.
- [Fields](https://docs.rs/enum.Fields.html)- `derive`or- `full`
- Data stored within an enum variant or struct.
- [FnArg](https://docs.rs/enum.FnArg.html)- `full`
- An argument in a function signature: the `n: usize`in`fn f(n: usize)`.
- [Foreign](https://docs.rs/enum.ForeignItem.html)- Item - `full`
- An item within an `extern`block.
- [Generic](https://docs.rs/enum.GenericArgument.html)- Argument - `derive`or- `full`
- An individual generic argument, like `'a`,`T`, or`Item = T`.
- [Generic](https://docs.rs/enum.GenericParam.html)- Param - `derive`or- `full`
- A generic type parameter, lifetime, or const generic: `T: Into<String>`,`'a: 'b`,`const LEN: usize`.
- [Impl](https://docs.rs/enum.ImplItem.html)- Item - `full`
- An item within an impl block.
- [Impl](https://docs.rs/enum.ImplRestriction.html)- Restriction - `full`
- Unused, but reserved for RFC 3323 restrictions.
- [Item](https://docs.rs/enum.Item.html)- `full`
- Things that can appear directly inside of a module or scope.
- [Lit](https://docs.rs/enum.Lit.html)
- A Rust literal such as a string or integer or boolean.
- [Macro](https://docs.rs/enum.MacroDelimiter.html)- Delimiter - `derive`or- `full`
- A grouping token that surrounds a macro body: `m!(...)`or`m!{...}`or`m![...]`.
- [Member](https://docs.rs/enum.Member.html)- `derive`or- `full`
- A struct or tuple struct field accessed in a struct literal or field expression.
- [Meta](https://docs.rs/enum.Meta.html)- `derive`or- `full`
- Content of a compile-time structured attribute.
- [Pat](https://docs.rs/enum.Pat.html)- `full`
- A pattern in a local binding, function signature, match expression, or various other places.
- [Path](https://docs.rs/enum.PathArguments.html)- Arguments - `derive`or- `full`
- Angle bracketed or parenthesized arguments of a path segment.
- [Pointer](https://docs.rs/enum.PointerMutability.html)- Mutability - `full`
- Mutability of a raw pointer (`*const T`,`*mut T`), in which non-mutable isn’t the implicit default.
- [Range](https://docs.rs/enum.RangeLimits.html)- Limits - `full`
- Limit types of a range, inclusive or exclusive.
- [Return](https://docs.rs/enum.ReturnType.html)- Type - `derive`or- `full`
- Return type of a function signature.
- [Static](https://docs.rs/enum.StaticMutability.html)- Mutability - `full`
- The mutability of an `Item::Static`or`ForeignItem::Static`.
- [Stmt](https://docs.rs/enum.Stmt.html)- `full`
- A statement, usually ending in a semicolon.
- [Trait](https://docs.rs/enum.TraitBoundModifier.html)- Bound - Modifier - `derive`or- `full`
- A modifier on a trait bound, currently only used for the `?`in`?Sized`.
- [Trait](https://docs.rs/enum.TraitItem.html)- Item - `full`
- An item declaration within the definition of a trait.
- [Type](https://docs.rs/enum.Type.html)- `derive`or- `full`
- The possible types that a Rust value could have.
- [Type](https://docs.rs/enum.TypeParamBound.html)- Param - Bound - `derive`or- `full`
- A trait or lifetime used as a bound on a type parameter.
- [UnOp](https://docs.rs/enum.UnOp.html)- `derive`or- `full`
- A unary operator: `*`,`!`,`-`.
- [UseTree](https://docs.rs/enum.UseTree.html)- `full`
- A suffix of an import tree in a `use`item:`Type as Renamed`or`*`.
- [Visibility](https://docs.rs/enum.Visibility.html)- `derive`or- `full`
- The visibility level of an item: inherited or `pub`or`pub(restricted)`.
- [Where](https://docs.rs/enum.WherePredicate.html)- Predicate - `derive`or- `full`
- A single predicate in a `where`clause:`T: Deserialize<'de>`.

# bindgen - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/bindgen/latest/target-redirect/bindgen/

## Expand description

Generate Rust bindings for C and C++ libraries.

Provide a C/C++ header file, receive Rust FFI code to call into C/C++ functions and use types defined in the header.

See the [ Builder](https://docs.rs/struct.Builder.html) struct for usage.

See the [Users Guide](https://rust-lang.github.io/rust-bindgen/) for
additional documentation.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [callbacks](https://docs.rs/callbacks/index.html)
- A public API for more fine-grained customization of bindgen behavior.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Bindings](https://docs.rs/struct.Bindings.html)
- Generated Rust bindings.
- [Builder](https://docs.rs/struct.Builder.html)
- Configure and generate Rust bindings for a C/C++ header.
- [Cargo](https://docs.rs/struct.CargoCallbacks.html)- Callbacks
- A `ParseCallbacks`implementation that will act on file includes by echoing a rerun-if-changed line and on env variable usage by echoing a rerun-if-env-changed line
- [Clang](https://docs.rs/struct.ClangVersion.html)- Version
- Extracted Clang version data
- [Codegen](https://docs.rs/struct.CodegenConfig.html)- Config
- A type used to indicate which kind of items we have to generate.
- [Rust](https://docs.rs/struct.RustTarget.html)- Target
- Represents the version of the Rust language to target.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Abi](https://docs.rs/enum.Abi.html)
- A valid rust ABI.
- [Alias](https://docs.rs/enum.AliasVariation.html)- Variation
- Enum for how aliases should be translated.
- [Bindgen](https://docs.rs/enum.BindgenError.html)- Error
- Error type for rust-bindgen.
- [Enum](https://docs.rs/enum.EnumVariation.html)- Variation
- A helper type that represents different enum variations.
- [Field](https://docs.rs/enum.FieldVisibilityKind.html)- Visibility - Kind
- What kind of visibility modifier should be used for a struct or field?
- [Formatter](https://docs.rs/enum.Formatter.html)
- Formatting tools that can be used to format the bindings
- [Macro](https://docs.rs/enum.MacroTypeVariation.html)- Type - Variation
- Enum for the default type of macro constants.
- [NonCopy](https://docs.rs/enum.NonCopyUnionStyle.html)- Union - Style
- Enum for how non-`Copy``union`s should be translated.
- [Rust](https://docs.rs/enum.RustEdition.html)- Edition
- Represents Rust Edition for the generated bindings

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [Cargo](https://docs.rs/constant.CargoCallbacks.html)- Callbacks - Deprecated
- Create a new `CargoCallbacks`value with`CargoCallbacks::rerun_on_header_files`
- [DEFAULT_](https://docs.rs/constant.DEFAULT_ANON_FIELDS_PREFIX.html)- ANON_ - FIELDS_ - PREFIX
- Default prefix for the anon fields.
- [LATEST_](https://docs.rs/constant.LATEST_STABLE_RUST.html)- STABLE_ - RUST
- Latest stable release of Rust that is supported by bindgen

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [builder](https://docs.rs/fn.builder.html)
- Construct a new `Builder`
- [clang_](https://docs.rs/fn.clang_version.html)- version
- Get the major and the minor semver numbers of Clang’s version

# About Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/about

Docs.rs is an
            [open source](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs)
            documentation host for crates of the
            [Rust Programming Language](https://www.rust-lang.org/).
            All libraries published to [crates.io](https://crates.io)
            are documented. If you just published a crate, your crate is likely
            still in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

            The source code of Docs.rs is available on
            [GitHub](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs). If
            you ever encounter an issue, don't hesitate to report it! (And
            thanks in advance!)

Currently running Docs.rs version is: **0.0.0 (964c90a45859fd8f9076e3cbe58470a5a4f4d4f7 2026-07-01 )**

Summaries of the documentation build processes [are available at /releases/](https://docs.rs/releases).

            JavaScript in support of documentation is allowed but not guaranteed to work on docs.rs. What that
            means: If you write documentation that inlines some JavaScript (like
            [KaTeX](https://katex.org/)), that's allowed, and
            will probably work today but may break in the future.

However, it's not allowed to put JavaScript or other content in docs published on docs.rs for the purpose of tracking visitors. For instance, adding Google Analytics scripts, tracking pixels, or site verification for services like Google Search Console. Crates that do this will have the relevant versions removed and may be blocked from docs.rs.

            Docs.rs is run and maintained by the [Docs.rs team](https://www.rust-lang.org/governance/teams/dev-tools#team-docs-rs).
            You can find us in #t-docs-rs on [Zulip](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/356853-t-docs-rs).

---

# Badges

Source: https://docs.rs/about/badges

Docs.rs no longer has its own badges. Consider using [shields.io](https://shields.io) instead.

# Builds

Source: https://docs.rs/about/builds

Docs.rs automatically builds documentation for crates released on [crates.io](https://crates.io/).
                It may take a while to build your crate, depending on how many crates are in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

                All crates are built in a sandbox using the nightly release of the Rust compiler.
                The current version in use is `rustc 1.98.0-nightly (4c9d2bfe4 2026-07-01)`.

                The README displayed on docs.rs follows Cargo’s `package.readme` rules.
                If `readme` is not set, docs.rs will look for `README.md`, `README.txt`, or `README` in the crate root.
                Set `readme = "path/to/file"` to use a custom file, `readme = true` to use `README.md`, or `readme = false` to disable the README.

                To recognize Docs.rs from your Rust code, you can test for the `docsrs` cfg, e.g.:

```
```
                To recognize Docs.rs from `build.rs` files, you can test for the environment variable `DOCS_RS`, e.g.:

`if var.is_ok `
              All targets other than `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` are cross-compiled. For implementation reasons, this is unlikely to change for the foreseeable future.

                You can configure how your crate is built by adding [package metadata](https://docs.rs/metadata) to your `Cargo.toml`, e.g.:

```
[]
 = ["--cfg", "my_cfg"]
```
`#[cfg(my_cfg)]` (not to be confused with `#[cfg(doc)]`) can be used for conditional compilation.
                This approach is also useful for setting
                When you start using docs.rs metadata or `#[cfg(docsrs)]` in your code, you might run into issues
                where your code builds fine locally but fails on docs.rs.
                To avoid this, you can add [ cargo docs-rs](https://github.com/dtolnay/cargo-docs-rs) to
                your test-suite.
                While it doesn't perfectly replicate our build environment, it can catch many common issues.

                The Docs.rs [README](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/blob/master/README.md#build-subcommand) describes how to build
                unpublished crate documentation locally using the same build environment as the Docs.rs build agent.

                Missing dependencies are a common reason for failed builds.
                Docs.rs dependencies are managed through
                [crates-build-env](https://github.com/rust-lang/crates-build-env).
                See [Forge](https://forge.rust-lang.org/docs-rs/add-dependencies.html) for how to add a dependency.

                Most of the sandbox is a read-only file system, including the source directory of your crate and its dependencies.
                If your `build.rs` generates files that are relevant for documentation, consider writing to the
                [cargo output directory](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/environment-variables.html#environment-variables-cargo-sets-for-crates),
                passed in the environment variable `OUT_DIR`.

All the builds are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The current limits are:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                If your build fails because it hit one of these limits, please
                [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                to get them increased for your crate.
                Since our build agent has finite resources, we have to consider each case individually. However, there are a few general policies:

If your crate fails to build for a reason not listed here, you can rebuild it from [crates.io](https://crates.io) website as you can see below:

Or you can [file an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues) if you think it's a **docs.rs** issue.

# Metadata

Source: https://docs.rs/about/metadata

You can customize docs.rs builds by defining `[package.metadata.docs.rs]`
		table in your crates' `Cargo.toml`.

The available configuration flags you can customize are:

```
[]
 = "test"
[]
# Features to pass to Cargo (default: [])
 = ["feature1", "feature2"]
# Whether to pass `--all-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Whether to pass `--no-default-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Target to test build on, used as the default landing page (default: "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu")
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
 = "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"
# Targets to build (default: see below)
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
#
# Default targets:
# - x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - aarch64-apple-darwin
# - x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
# - aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - i686-pc-windows-msvc
#
# Set this to `[]` to only build the default target.
#
# If `default-target` is unset, the first element of `targets` is treated as the default target.
# Otherwise, these `targets` are built in addition to the default target.
# If both `default-target` and `targets` are unset,
#   all tier-one targets will be built and `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` will be used as the default target.
 = ["aarch64-apple-darwin", "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc"]
# If you want to instead add another target without overwriting the default ones:
 = ["i686-apple-darwin"]
# Additional `RUSTFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustc-arg"]
# Additional `RUSTDOCFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustdoc-arg"]
# List of command line arguments for `cargo`.
#
# These cannot be a subcommand, they may only be options.
 = ["-Z", "build-std"]
```

# Shorthand URLs

Source: https://docs.rs/about/redirections

Docs.rs uses semver to parse URLs. You can use this feature to access
            crates' documentation easily. Example of URL redirections for
            `clap` crate:

| URL | Redirects to documentation of |
|---|---|
| [docs.rs/clap](https://docs.rs/clap) | Latest version of clap |
| [docs.rs/clap::Command](https://docs.rs/clap::Command) | Latest version of clap, and search for "Command" within the crate |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2) | 2.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2.9](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2.9) | 2.9.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/2.9.3](https://docs.rs/clap/2.9.3) | 2.9.3 version (you don't need `=`unlike semver) |
| [docs.rs/clap/*](https://docs.rs/clap/*) | Latest version of this page (if it still exists). "latest" or "newest" work as well as `*`. |

---

# Download

Source: https://docs.rs/about/download

docs.rs stores the `rustdoc` output in a ZIP file.

                These archives can be used as a base for further processing of
                the documentation for offline readers like Dash or Zeal.
                **They are not directly usable for offline documentation.**

The download is possible for specific or semantic versions:

But also viaTo unpack the ZIP file you need any zip utility that supports PKZIP version 4.6 and BZIP2 & Deflate compression.

The archives will contain all the documentation HTML files for all targets and CSS/JS assets that are specific to the build. The default target will be found at the root, and other targets each in its own subfolder.

                Docs.rs is running rustdoc with `--static-root-path "/-/rustdoc.static/"`,
                which leads to all references to static assets breaking if they are not
                available under that path. Older builds used `--static-root-path "/"`, which
                means you will have to handle both.

                Since we're also adding `--emit=invocation-specific` to our build
                the archives will *not* contain any static assets that are specific to the
                toolchain. For now these will have to be downloaded file-by-file directly
                from docs.rs.

---

# Rustdoc JSON

Source: https://docs.rs/about/rustdoc-json

docs.rs builds & hosts the [ rustdoc JSON](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustdoc/unstable-features.html#json-output) output.

This structured version of the documentation can be used for inspecting the docs and types of the crate in a programmatic way.

                The JSON file you're downloading might have been built with an older version of `rustdoc`
                so you might have to check the `format_version` attribute to determine how to parse the structure.
                The [ rustdoc-types](https://docs.rs/rustdoc-types/) crate helps with this.

**
                We started building rustdoc JSON on 2025-05-23. So any release before that won't have a download
                available until our rebuilds reached that release.
            **

                The download URLs can be generic or specific, depending on what you need. In case of rebuilds we
                also keep old format versions around. **Until we rebuilt all releases, we might return
                a `404 NOT FOUND` for some.**

By default we use `zstd` compression, which is more space efficient and faster to decompress. For more limited environments we also started supporting `gzip` compression. You can receive gzip by adding `.gz` to the given URL.

Here some URL examples you can use.

| URL | Redirects to JSON download of |
|---|---|
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json) | latest version, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz) | latest version, default target, latest format-version, gzip compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42) | latest version, default target, format-version 42 |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json.zst](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json.zst) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version, zstd compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json) | latest version, windows target, latest format-version |

# reifydb_rql - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/reifydb-rql/0.7.0/reifydb_rql/

## Expand description

ReifyDB Query Language: lexer, parser, AST, logical and physical planning, optimisation, and the instruction stream consumed by the engine VM. This is the full pipeline that turns a source string into something executable.

The crate exposes the AST shape so external tooling (formatters, linters, the explain renderer) can inspect queries without re-parsing, and exposes a stable fingerprint over compiled plans that the engine uses for plan caching. Diagnostics produced here carry source-fragment context so user-visible failures can point at the offending span.

Invariant: planner output is decoupled from any specific storage backend. The physical plan is expressed in terms
of `core::interface/` traits; concrete backend selection happens later, in the engine. Reaching into a specific
backend from inside the planner couples this crate to the storage tier and breaks the layering that lets `core`
avoid cycles.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [ast](https://docs.rs/ast/index.html)
- Abstract syntax tree for RQL. The parser entry point `parse_str`tokenises a source string and emits an`AstStatement`tree allocated in a bump arena tied to the source lifetime, so spans inside the AST can refer back to fragments of the original text without copying.
- [bump](https://docs.rs/bump/index.html)
- [compiler](https://docs.rs/compiler/index.html)
- [diagnostic](https://docs.rs/diagnostic/index.html)
- [error](https://docs.rs/error/index.html)
- [expression](https://docs.rs/expression/index.html)
- Planner-side expression representation. Mirrors the AST’s expression shapes but in a form that has been type-checked, name-resolved, and stripped of source-only details. The engine consumes these expressions to evaluate filters, projections, and join conditions; routine call resolution and JSON-path navigation are part of this representation rather than the runtime.
- [fingerprint](https://docs.rs/fingerprint/index.html)
- [flow](https://docs.rs/flow/index.html)
- RQL planning for CREATE FLOW. Analyses the source query, builds the operator graph, plans each operator
against the catalog, and produces the persisted flow definition the engine hands to `sub-flow`at runtime. Dataflow shape - which operator depends on which - is settled here, not in the streaming runtime.
- [instruction](https://docs.rs/instruction/index.html)
- [nodes](https://docs.rs/nodes/index.html)
- [optimize](https://docs.rs/optimize/index.html)
- Physical-plan post-passes. Walks the lowered plan and applies expression-level rewrites - constant folding,
projection simplification - that were not worth doing during logical compilation. New optimisations register
through the same `walk_expressions_mut`interface so they can be composed without re-traversing the plan once per pass.
- [plan](https://docs.rs/plan/index.html)
- Two-stage planner. `compile_logical`resolves names, type-checks, and produces a logical plan in terms of`core::interface/`primitives;`compile_physical`lowers that into the executable shape the engine VM consumes.`plan_with_policy`is the variant that interleaves a policy-injection pass between the two stages so read filters land before the physical lowering.
- [query](https://docs.rs/query/index.html)
- [token](https://docs.rs/token/index.html)

# null_sigma - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/null-sigma/0.1.0/null_sigma/

## Expand description

High-performance [Sigma](https://sigmahq.io) rule evaluation engine.

Parse Sigma rules from YAML once, compile them into an optimised internal
representation, then evaluate streams of security events against the full
rule set at **449 000+ events/second × 1 000 rules on a single core**
(Apple M4, release, Criterion-measured).

[§](https://docs.rs#quick-start)Quick Start

```
use null_sigma::SigmaEngine;
use std::collections::HashMap;
let yaml = r#"
title: Detect Encoded PowerShell
logsource: {}
detection:
    sel:
        CommandLine|contains: '-EncodedCommand'
    condition: sel
"#;
let mut engine = SigmaEngine::new();
engine.load_rule(yaml).unwrap();
let mut event = HashMap::new();
event.insert("CommandLine".to_string(), "powershell -EncodedCommand abc".to_string());
let matches = engine.evaluate_event(&event);
assert_eq!(matches.len(), 1);
assert_eq!(matches[0].rule_title, "Detect Encoded PowerShell");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#architecture)Architecture

| Module | Role |
|---|---|
| `types` | Core type system: `SigmaRule`,`SeverityLevel`,`ValueModifier`, … |
| `parser` | YAML → `SigmaRule`with full validation |
| `condition` | Condition expression → boolean AST |
| `matcher` | Event field matching — all 15 Sigma modifiers |
| `fieldmap` | Sigma field-name translation |
| `engine` | Multi-rule evaluation with Aho-Corasick optimisation |

- Condition expression compiler: Sigma condition strings → boolean AST
(`condition::ConditionNode`
- [engine](https://docs.rs/engine/index.html)
- Multi-rule evaluation engine with Aho-Corasick batch prefilter and cache-friendly hot/cold struct split.

- Core type system: `SigmaRule`,`SeverityLevel`,`ValueModifier`, and all supporting data types used throughout the crate.

# hotspots-cli 1.27.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/hotspots-cli/1.27.0

# Hotspots

**Website:** [https://hotspots.dev](https://hotspots.dev)  |  **Docs:** [https://docs.hotspots.dev](https://docs.hotspots.dev)  |  **Crates.io:**

**Install:** `brew install Stephen-Collins-tech/tap/hotspots`  |  `npm install -g @stephencollinstech/hotspots`  |  `pip install hotspots-cli`  |  `cargo install hotspots-cli`

**Find the code that's actually causing problems.**

Your codebase has thousands of functions. Some are messy but never break. Others are complex AND change constantly — those are your **hotspots**, the 20% of code causing 80% of your bugs, incidents, and slowdowns.

## Install

` | `Windows: download the binary from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/Stephen-Collins-tech/hotspots/releases/latest).

Verify: `hotspots --version`

**GitHub Action:**

```
- uses: Stephen-Collins-tech/hotspots/action@v1
  with:
    github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
```
## Quick Start

```
# Find your hotspots
# Critical (LRS ≥ 9.0):
# processPlanUpgrade    src/api/billing.ts:142    LRS 12.4  CC 15  ND 4  FO 8  NS 3
#
# High (6.0 ≤ LRS < 9.0):
# validateSession       src/auth/session.ts:67    LRS 9.8   CC 11  ND 3  FO 7  NS 2
```
**Critical** = refactor now. **High** = refactor next time you touch it. **Moderate** = block increases. **Low** = leave it alone.

### Common commands

```
# Per-function explanations with refactoring advice
# Block complexity regressions in CI
# Compare any two git refs
# Interactive HTML report
# JSON for tooling/AI
# Track trends over time
# Train a repo-specific ranker from your bug history
```
## How It Works

Hotspots computes a **Local Risk Score (LRS)** per function from four structural metrics:

| Metric | What it measures |
|---|---|
| CC— Cyclomatic Complexity | Independent decision paths (if/loop/catch/&&/||) |
| ND— Nesting Depth | Maximum depth of nested control structures |
| FO— Fan-Out | Distinct functions called |
| NS— Non-Structured Exits | Early returns, throws, breaks |

```
LRS = 1.0×R_cc + 0.8×R_nd + 0.6×R_fo + 0.7×R_ns
```
where each component is log-scaled and capped to prevent outliers from dominating.

In **snapshot mode**, LRS is combined with git history (churn, touch frequency, recency) and call graph metrics (fan-in, PageRank, SCC membership) to compute an **Activity Risk Score** and place each function in a triage quadrant:

| Quadrant | Complexity | Activity | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fire` | High | High | Refactor now |
| `debt` | High | Low | Schedule before next push |
| `watch` | Low | High | Monitor |
| `ok` | Low | Low | Leave it alone |

**Risk bands:** Low (< 3) · Moderate (3–6) · High (6–9) · Critical (≥ 9)

## Supported Languages

TypeScript · JavaScript · Go · Python · Rust · Java · C/C headers · C# · Vue

All 12 file extensions (`.ts`, `.tsx`, `.mts`, `.cts`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.go`, `.py`, `.rs`, `.java`, `.c`, `.h`, `.cs`, `.vue`) work out of the box.

## CI/CD Integration

### GitHub Action (zero config)

```
name: Hotspots
on:
jobs:
  analyze:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: Stephen-Collins-tech/hotspots-action@v1
        with:
          github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
```
Posts PR comments, generates HTML reports, fails builds on policy violations.

### Manual CI

```
# Fail CI if new critical functions introduced or LRS increases ≥ 1.0
```
Exit code 1 on blocking violations, 0 on warnings only.

## Key Features

**Policy engine** — blocks: new critical-risk functions, LRS regressions ≥ 1.0, net repo regression ≥ 5.0. Warns: approaching thresholds, rapid growth > 50%.

**Driver labels** — each function gets a primary diagnosis: `high_complexity`, `deep_nesting`, `exit_heavy`, `high_churn_low_cc`, `high_fanout_churning`, `high_fanin_complex`, `cyclic_dep`, or `composite`.

**Pattern detection** — 13 named patterns in two tiers: structural (always, e.g. `complex_branching`, `god_function`) and enriched (snapshot mode, e.g. `churn_magnet`, `cyclic_hub`, `volatile_god`).

**Suppression comments** — exclude functions from CI failures while keeping them visible:

```
// hotspots-ignore: legacy payment processor, rewrite scheduled Q2 2026
function legacyBillingLogic() { ... }
```
**Trained ranker** — fit a RandomForest from your repo's bug-fix history:

**Output formats** — `text` (terminal), `json` (machine), `jsonl` (streaming), `html` (interactive), `sarif` (GitHub Code Scanning).

**Configuration** — `.hotspotsrc.json` in project root (auto-discovered):

```
```
## Documentation

- [docs/USAGE.md](https://docs.rs/docs/USAGE.md)— workflows, CI setup, output formats, policy engine, suppression, training, snapshot management
- [docs/REFERENCE.md](https://docs.rs/docs/REFERENCE.md)— complete CLI reference, all flags, config options, JSON schema, metrics formula
- [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](https://docs.rs/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)— system design, analysis pipeline, invariants, design decisions
- [docs/CONTRIBUTING.md](https://docs.rs/docs/CONTRIBUTING.md)— dev setup, adding languages, release process

## Why Hotspots?

**vs ESLint complexity rules** — ESLint checks one metric in isolation with no git context. Hotspots combines four metrics, git history, and call graph topology into a single prioritized list.

**vs SonarQube / CodeClimate** — Enterprise platforms requiring server infrastructure. Hotspots is a single binary, zero config, works offline, results in seconds.

**vs code reviews** — Reviews catch complexity subjectively and miss gradual drift. Hotspots enforces objective thresholds automatically on every commit.

## Contributing

- Bug reports: [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/Stephen-Collins-tech/hotspots/issues)
- Feature requests: [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/Stephen-Collins-tech/hotspots/discussions)
- PRs: see [docs/CONTRIBUTING.md](https://docs.rs/docs/CONTRIBUTING.md)

# rustnetconf - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rustnetconf/0.12.3/rustnetconf/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#rustnetconf)rustnetconf

An async-first NETCONF 1.0/1.1 client library for Rust.

Built on [tokio](https://tokio.rs) and [russh](https://crates.io/crates/russh)
for high-performance, memory-safe network device management.

[§](https://docs.rs#quick-start)Quick Start

```
use rustnetconf::{Client, Datastore};
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let mut client = Client::connect("10.0.0.1:830")
        .username("admin")
        .password("secret")
        .connect()
        .await?;
    let config = client.get_config(Datastore::Running).await?;
    println!("{config}");
    client.close_session().await?;
    Ok(())
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#architecture)Architecture

`Client (thin wrapper) → Session (protocol state) → Framing → Transport (SSH)`See [ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/fastrevmd-lab/rustnetconf/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md)
for full design details.

# bp_runtime - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bp-runtime/0.28.0/bp_runtime/

## Expand description

Primitives that may be used at (bridges) runtime level.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use sp_runtime::`- [paste](https://docs.rs/paste/1.0.15/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/paste/index.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [extensions](https://docs.rs/extensions/index.html)
- Primitives that may be used for creating signed extensions for indirect runtimes.
- [messages](https://docs.rs/messages/index.html)
- Primitives that may be used by different message delivery and dispatch mechanisms.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [decl_](https://docs.rs/macro.decl_bridge_finality_runtime_apis.html)- bridge_ - finality_ - runtime_ - apis
- Convenience macro that declares bridge finality runtime apis and related constants for a chain. This includes:
- [decl_](https://docs.rs/macro.decl_bridge_messages_runtime_apis.html)- bridge_ - messages_ - runtime_ - apis
- Convenience macro that declares bridge messages runtime apis and related constants for a chain. This includes:
- [decl_](https://docs.rs/macro.decl_bridge_runtime_apis.html)- bridge_ - runtime_ - apis
- Convenience macro that declares bridge finality runtime apis, bridge messages runtime apis
and related constants for a chain.
The name of the chain has to be specified in snake case (e.g. `bridge_hub_polkadot`).
- [generate_](https://docs.rs/macro.generate_static_str_provider.html)- static_ - str_ - provider
- A macro that generates `StaticStrProvider`with the string set to its stringified argument.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- A bounded runtime storage value.

- Generic header Id.

- Adapter for `Get<u32>`to access`PARACHAIN_ID`from`trait Parachain`
- [PreComputed](https://docs.rs/struct.PreComputedSize.html)- Size
- Pre-computed size.
- [Storage](https://docs.rs/struct.StorageProofChecker.html)- Proof - Checker
- This struct is used to read storage values from a subset of a Merklized database. The “proof” is a subset of the nodes in the Merkle structure of the database, so that it provides authentication against a known Merkle root as well as the values in the database themselves.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Basic](https://docs.rs/enum.BasicOperatingMode.html)- Operating - Mode
- Basic operating modes for a bridges module (Normal/Halted).
- [Encoded](https://docs.rs/enum.EncodedOrDecodedCall.html)- OrDecoded - Call
- Chain call, that is either SCALE-encoded, or decoded.
- [Owned](https://docs.rs/enum.OwnedBridgeModuleError.html)- Bridge - Module - Error

- [Transaction](https://docs.rs/enum.TransactionEra.html)- Era
- Era of specific transaction.

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/rustnetconf-cli/0.3.3

rustnetconf-cli-0.3.3 is not a library.

                rustnetconf CLI — Terraform-like declarative network config management.

```
netconf plan <device>       Show what would change
netconf apply <device>      Apply changes with confirmed-commit
netconf confirm <device>    Make changes permanent
netconf rollback <device>   Revert to saved state
netconf get <device>        Fetch running config
netconf validate <device>   Dry-run validation
netconf init                Create project skeleton
```

# reifydb_cdc - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/reifydb-cdc/0.7.0/reifydb_cdc/

## Expand description

Change Data Capture: durable record of every committed write, ordered, addressable, and consumable by external systems. The transaction layer hands committed deltas here at commit time; this crate persists them, exposes the consumer-side cursor APIs that downstream replication, subscriptions, and external sinks read from, and runs the background compactor that prunes records past retention.

Producers and consumers are decoupled - a write only needs to be persisted before the transaction returns; the consumer side can fall arbitrarily far behind and catch up later. Storage is pluggable so the same protocol can be backed by SQLite for embedded deployments and by a horizontally scaled log for production.

Invariant: a CDC record published for a transaction reflects exactly the deltas that were committed under that transaction id, in the order the engine produced them. Reordering or dropping deltas inside CDC desynchronises replicas and subscriptions from the source of truth.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [compact](https://docs.rs/compact/index.html)
- [consume](https://docs.rs/consume/index.html)
- Consumer side of the CDC stream. A consumer registers with the host actor, polls for new records past its checkpoint, and advances a watermark so the producer side knows what is safe to compact. Each subscriber holds its own checkpoint independently; a slow consumer never blocks a fast one.
- [error](https://docs.rs/error/index.html)
- [produce](https://docs.rs/produce/index.html)
- Producer side of the CDC stream. The transaction layer hands committed deltas here at commit time; the producer encodes them into CDC records, persists them to storage, and advances the publisher watermark so consumers can observe the new commit boundary. Decoding lives next to producing so the round-trip is symmetric.
- [storage](https://docs.rs/storage/index.html)
- Pluggable backing store for the CDC log. The in-memory implementation is the testing default; SQLite is the durable default for production deployments. Both implement the same trait surface so the producer and consumer sides are agnostic to which is configured.
- [testing](https://docs.rs/testing/index.html)

---

# reifydb_auth - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/reifydb-auth/0.7.0/reifydb_auth/

## Expand description

Authentication: turning a wire-level credential into a verified `IdentityId` the rest of the system can attach
to a transaction. The crate owns the registry of supported authentication methods, the challenge-response state
machine for methods that need it, and the service handle the server tiers route incoming sessions through.

Authorisation - what an identity is allowed to do once authenticated - is not in this crate; that is the policy engine’s responsibility. The split exists so a deployment can swap out authentication methods (token, password, external IDP) without touching the policy enforcement path.

Invariant: a successful authentication produces an `IdentityId` that resolves through the catalog to a real,
non-revoked identity. Anything that mints an `IdentityId` outside this crate (test fixtures aside) bypasses
revocation and method requirements and is a security regression.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [challenge](https://docs.rs/challenge/index.html)
- [error](https://docs.rs/error/index.html)
- [method](https://docs.rs/method/index.html)
- Authentication method implementations. Each method is self-contained - it owns its credential format,
verification logic, and challenge state - and registers with the `registry/`so the service can pick the right one for an incoming request. Adding a new method (a new IDP, a new key type) means writing one of these modules and registering it; the rest of the auth surface is method-agnostic.
- [registry](https://docs.rs/registry/index.html)
- [service](https://docs.rs/service/index.html)
- Auth service handle wired up by the runtime. Owns the catalog and admin-transaction handles needed to verify credentials, mint tokens, and load identities; exposes the high-level “authenticate this request” entry point that server transports invoke. Per-method specifics (token, Solana key) sit in submodules so the public surface stays method-agnostic.

---

# reifydb_catalog - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/reifydb-catalog/0.7.0/reifydb_catalog/

## Expand description

Concrete implementation of the catalog object hierarchy declared by `core::interface::catalog`. Owns the on-disk
representation of namespaces, tables, views, flows, identities, policies, sequences, tokens, tests, and the system
objects ReifyDB self-hosts; resolves names through the resolved-name machinery; and provides the materialized
views that the engine reads to plan and execute queries.

Catalog reads ride on a regular transaction; catalog writes go through the admin transaction so DDL and identity mutations are isolated from concurrent OLTP traffic and emit their own change records. Bootstrap installs the system namespace and the seed identities the rest of the system depends on; vtable exposes catalog state to RQL as queryable virtual tables.

Invariant: persisted catalog ids (namespace id, table id, identity id, etc.) are stable across reboots; ephemeral per-boot ids exist for in-memory resolution but never round-trip through storage. Mixing the two leaves dangling references when the process restarts.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [bootstrap](https://docs.rs/bootstrap/index.html)
- Catalog bootstrap. Runs at startup, installs the system namespace, the seed identities (root, the system background actors), and any built-in shapes the engine needs before it can serve traffic. On a fresh database the bootstrap writes the initial state; on a recovered database it idempotently confirms the same objects exist and matches versions.
- [cache](https://docs.rs/cache/index.html)
- In-memory materialised view of the catalog: every catalog object the running engine has seen, indexed for fast lookup by id and qualified name. The materialised view is loaded at boot, kept in sync with catalog mutations through change events, and is what the engine, planner, and policy evaluator query when they need catalog state on the hot path.
- [catalog](https://docs.rs/catalog/index.html)
- Per-object-type catalog operations: every kind of catalog object has a sibling module here that knows how to create, look up, list, modify, and delete instances of that object. Each follows the same shape - admin-only mutations, transactional reads, name-and-id resolution - so adding a new catalog object kind is mostly a mechanical exercise.
- [change](https://docs.rs/change/index.html)
- Catalog change handlers. When a CDC record describes a catalog mutation, the right handler here decodes the change, applies it to the materialised catalog view, and surfaces it through the catalog change events the rest of the workspace listens for. Each catalog object kind has a handler that knows the layout of its rows and how to fold an insert/update/delete into the materialised state.
- [error](https://docs.rs/error/index.html)
- [interceptor](https://docs.rs/interceptor/index.html)
- [shape](https://docs.rs/shape/index.html)
- Decoders for the encoded-row layouts catalog shapes use. Each shape (table, ringbuffer, series, dictionary) has a different on-disk record format; this module owns the byte-level decoding so the rest of the catalog code can work with typed values instead of raw bytes.
- [store](https://docs.rs/store/index.html)
- Storage-facing implementation of catalog persistence. Each object kind has a sibling module here that owns the
`EncodedKey`layout and the (de)serialisation between the typed catalog object and its on-disk bytes. The higher-level catalog operations in`catalog/`go through this layer rather than reaching into a backend directly, so adding a new store backend means re-implementing this trait surface, not the entire catalog.
- [system](https://docs.rs/system/index.html)
- Self-hosted system tables. Every catalog object kind ReifyDB stores about itself - identities, namespaces,
columns, policies, flows, sequences, the system event log, and so on - is exposed here as a virtual table so
it can be queried with regular RQL. The vtable definitions registered through this module are what `SELECT * FROM system.<thing>`reads from.
- [test_](https://docs.rs/test_utils/index.html)- utils
- [vtable](https://docs.rs/vtable/index.html)
- Virtual-table runtime. Each system table the catalog exposes through `system/`is backed by a vtable handler registered here; when an RQL query reads from one of those tables, the engine dispatches to the matching handler which materialises the rows from in-memory catalog state. No persisted bytes back system tables, only a snapshot of what the materialised catalog already knows.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [create_](https://docs.rs/fn.create_token.html)- token
- [drop_](https://docs.rs/fn.drop_expired_tokens.html)- expired_ - tokens
- [drop_](https://docs.rs/fn.drop_flow_by_name.html)- flow_ - by_ - name
- [drop_](https://docs.rs/fn.drop_token.html)- token
- [drop_](https://docs.rs/fn.drop_tokens_by_identity.html)- tokens_ - by_ - identity
- [find_](https://docs.rs/fn.find_token_by_value.html)- token_ - by_ - value

# cli_engine - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cli-engine/0.3.5/cli_engine/

## Expand description

Build consistent, domain-oriented CLIs with a small amount of Rust.

`cli_engine` provides the shared pieces that most CLI tools need:
command registration, authentication provider routing, authorization hooks,
audit and activity hooks, structured output, output schemas, guides, search,
command tree rendering, busybox-style multi-call (`argv[0]`) dispatch, and
authenticated HTTP transport helpers.

The intended shape is:

- Each team owns one or more `Module`
- A module registers noun-based `GroupSpec`
- Groups contain verb-like `CommandSpec`
- Command handlers stay focused on domain behavior while `Middleware`

[§](https://docs.rs#quick-start)Quick Start

```
use clap::Arg;
use cli_engine::{
    BuildInfo, Cli, CliConfig, CommandSpec, GroupSpec, Module,
    RuntimeCommandSpec, RuntimeGroupSpec,
};
use serde_json::json;
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> std::process::ExitCode {
    let list = RuntimeCommandSpec::new(
        CommandSpec::new("list", "List projects")
            .with_system("projects-api")
            .with_default_fields("id,name,status")
            .with_arg(Arg::new("team").long("team").required(true))
            .no_auth(true),
        async |_credential, args| {
            let team = args
                .get("team")
                .and_then(|value| value.as_str())
                .unwrap_or_default();
            Ok(cli_engine::CommandResult::new(json!([
                { "id": "p1", "name": "Portal", "status": "active", "team": team }
            ])))
        },
    );
    let module = Module::new("Platform Systems", move |_context| {
        RuntimeGroupSpec::new(GroupSpec::new("project", "Manage projects"))
            .with_command(list.clone())
    });
    let cli = Cli::new(
        CliConfig::new("example", "Example cli-engine application", "example")
            .with_build(BuildInfo::new(env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")))
            .with_module(module),
    );
    cli.execute().await
}
```
Command paths are colon-separated (`project:list`) for policy, audit,
schema, and authorization compatibility with existing CLI ecosystems.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

# tracing_gum - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/tracing-gum/26.0.0/tracing_gum/

## Expand description

A wrapper around `tracing` macros, to provide semi automatic
`traceID` annotation without codebase turnover.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

The API follows the [ tracing
API](https://docs.rs/tracing/latest/tracing/index.html), but the docs contain
more detail than you probably need to know, so here’s the quick version.

Most common usage is of the form:

```
gum::warn!(
    target: LOG_TARGET,
    worker_pid = %idle_worker.pid,
    ?error,
    "failed to send a handshake to the spawned worker",
);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#log-levels)Log levels

All of the [ tracing macros](https://docs.rs/tracing/latest/tracing/index.html#macros) are available.
In decreasing order of priority they are:

- `error!`
- `warn!`
- `info!`
- `debug!`
- `trace!`

[§](https://docs.rs#target)`target`

The `LOG_TARGET` should be defined once per crate, e.g.:

`const LOG_TARGET: &str = "parachain::pvf";`This should be of the form `<target>::<subtarget>`, where the `::<subtarget>` is optional.

The target and subtarget are used when debugging by specializing the Grafana Loki query to filter specific subsystem logs. The more specific the query is the better when approaching the query response limit.

[§](https://docs.rs#fields-1)Fields

Here’s the rundown on how fields work:

- Fields on spans and events are specified using the `syntax field_name = field_value`.
- Local variables may be used as field values without an assignment, similar to struct initializers.
- The `?`sigil is shorthand that specifies a field should be recorded using its`fmt::Debug`implementation.
- The `%`sigil operates similarly, but indicates that the value should be recorded using its`fmt::Display`implementation.

For full details, again see [the tracing
docs](https://docs.rs/tracing/latest/tracing/index.html#recording-fields).

[§](https://docs.rs#viewing-traces)Viewing traces

When testing,

`sp_tracing::init_for_tests();`should enable all trace logs.

Alternatively, you can do:

`sp_tracing::try_init_simple();`On the command line you specify `RUST_LOG` with the desired target and trace level:

`RUST_LOG=parachain::pvf=trace cargo test`On the other hand if you want all `parachain` logs, specify `parachain=trace`, which will also
include logs from `parachain::pvf` and other subtargets.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [event](https://docs.rs/event/index.html)
- Events represent single points in time during the execution of a program.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [debug](https://docs.rs/macro.debug.html)
- Print a debug level message.
- [enabled](https://docs.rs/macro.enabled.html)
- Checks whether a span or event is [enabled](https://docs.rs/tracing-core/0.1.36/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/tracing_core/subscriber/trait.Subscriber.html#tymethod.enabled)based on the provided[metadata](https://docs.rs/tracing-core/0.1.36/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/tracing_core/metadata/struct.Metadata.html).
- [error](https://docs.rs/macro.error.html)
- Print an error message.
- [event](https://docs.rs/macro.event.html)
- Constructs a new `Event`.
- [info](https://docs.rs/macro.info.html)
- Print a info level message.
- [trace](https://docs.rs/macro.trace.html)
- Print a trace level message.
- [warn](https://docs.rs/macro.warn.html)
- Print a warning level message.
- [warn_](https://docs.rs/macro.warn_if_frequent.html)- if_ - frequent
- Print a warning or debug level message depending on their frequency

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Freq](https://docs.rs/struct.Freq.html)
- Utility struct to compare the rate of its own calls.
- [Level](https://docs.rs/struct.Level.html)
- Describes the level of verbosity of a span or event.

# reifydb_transaction - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/reifydb-transaction/0.7.0/reifydb_transaction/

## Expand description

Transactional layer over the storage tier: opens a read or read-write transaction, accumulates deltas, validates
conflicts, and commits atomically. The crate offers two flavours - a multi-version path for OLTP traffic that needs
snapshot isolation, and a single-version path for workloads where versioning would only add overhead - and exposes
both behind a uniform `Transaction` handle that the engine threads through every request.

Every change recorded inside a transaction is captured as a delta, surfaced through the change accumulator, and published downstream so CDC consumers, replication, and subscriptions observe the same write set the engine just committed. Interceptors hook the commit boundary and let policy, audit, and consistency checks run with full visibility into what is about to be written.

Invariant: a `TransactionId` is unique system-wide and monotonic via Uuid7; downstream consumers (CDC, replication,
subscriptions) order events by transaction id, so reusing or back-dating an id silently breaks consumer
consistency.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [change](https://docs.rs/change/index.html)
- [change_](https://docs.rs/change_accumulator/index.html)- accumulator
- [delta](https://docs.rs/delta/index.html)
- [dictionary](https://docs.rs/dictionary/index.html)
- [error](https://docs.rs/error/index.html)
- [interceptor](https://docs.rs/interceptor/index.html)
- [multi](https://docs.rs/multi/index.html)
- Multi-version transactional path. Owns the conflict detector that decides whether a write transaction can commit at its read snapshot, the watermark machinery that tracks the lowest still-readable version for GC, and the oracle that hands out commit versions in monotonic order. Read, write, and replica transaction bodies are the three concrete shapes a multi-version transaction can take.
- [single](https://docs.rs/single/index.html)
- Single-version transactional path. No snapshot isolation, no conflict detector, no version oracle - a write transaction sees its own buffered changes and commits them atomically against the underlying single-version store. Suitable for OLTP workloads that do not need history and are willing to take last-writer-wins semantics between concurrent writers in exchange for less overhead.
- [transaction](https://docs.rs/transaction/index.html)
- Public `Transaction`handle. Wraps either a single-version or multi-version transaction body in a uniform shape so callers in the engine, planner, and policy layers do not branch on backend. Exposes the get/set/range primitives, delta accumulation, commit, the shape-resolution helpers, and the admin-only mutations the catalog tier needs.

---

# bindgen 0.72.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/bindgen/0.72.1

`bindgen`

`bindgen` automatically generates Rust FFI bindings to C (and some C++) libraries.

For example, given the C header `doggo.h`:

```
typedef struct Doggo  Doggo;
void ;
```
`bindgen` produces Rust FFI code allowing you to call into the `doggo` library's
functions and use its types:

```
/* automatically generated by rust-bindgen 0.99.9 */
extern "C"
```
## Users Guide

## MSRV

The `bindgen` minimum supported Rust version is **1.70.0**.

The `bindgen-cli` minimum supported Rust version is **1.70.0**.

No MSRV bump policy has been established yet, so MSRV may increase in any release.

The MSRV is the minimum Rust version that can be used to *compile* each crate. However, `bindgen` and `bindgen-cli` can generate bindings that are compatible with Rust versions below the current MSRV.

Most of the time, the `bindgen-cli` crate will have a more recent MSRV than `bindgen` as crates such as `clap` require it.

## API Reference

## Environment Variables

In addition to the [library API](https://docs.rs/bindgen) and [executable command-line API](https://rust-lang.github.io/rust-bindgen/command-line-usage.html),
`bindgen` can be controlled through environment variables.

End-users should set these environment variables to modify `bindgen`'s behavior without modifying the source code of direct consumers of `bindgen`.

- `BINDGEN_EXTRA_CLANG_ARGS`: extra arguments to pass to- `clang`- Arguments are whitespace-separated
- Use shell-style quoting to pass through whitespace
- Examples:
- Specify alternate sysroot: `--sysroot=/path/to/sysroot`
- Add include search path with spaces: `-I"/path/with spaces"`

- Specify alternate sysroot:

- `BINDGEN_EXTRA_CLANG_ARGS_<TARGET>`: similar to- `BINDGEN_EXTRA_CLANG_ARGS`, but used to set per-target arguments to pass to clang. Useful to set system include directories in a target-specific way in cross-compilation environments with multiple targets. Has precedence over- `BINDGEN_EXTRA_CLANG_ARGS`.

Additionally, `bindgen` uses `libclang` to parse C and C++ header files.
To modify how `bindgen` searches for `libclang`, see the [ clang-sys documentation](https://github.com/KyleMayes/clang-sys#environment-variables).
For more details on how

`bindgen` uses `libclang`, see the [.](https://rust-lang.github.io/rust-bindgen/requirements.html#clang)

`bindgen` users guide## Releases

We don't follow a specific release calendar, but if you need a release please
file an issue requesting that (ping `@emilio` for increased effectiveness).

---

# bindgen - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/bindgen/0.72.1/target-redirect/bindgen/

## Expand description

Generate Rust bindings for C and C++ libraries.

Provide a C/C++ header file, receive Rust FFI code to call into C/C++ functions and use types defined in the header.

See the [ Builder](https://docs.rs/struct.Builder.html) struct for usage.

See the [Users Guide](https://rust-lang.github.io/rust-bindgen/) for
additional documentation.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [callbacks](https://docs.rs/callbacks/index.html)
- A public API for more fine-grained customization of bindgen behavior.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Bindings](https://docs.rs/struct.Bindings.html)
- Generated Rust bindings.
- [Builder](https://docs.rs/struct.Builder.html)
- Configure and generate Rust bindings for a C/C++ header.
- [Cargo](https://docs.rs/struct.CargoCallbacks.html)- Callbacks
- A `ParseCallbacks`implementation that will act on file includes by echoing a rerun-if-changed line and on env variable usage by echoing a rerun-if-env-changed line
- [Clang](https://docs.rs/struct.ClangVersion.html)- Version
- Extracted Clang version data
- [Codegen](https://docs.rs/struct.CodegenConfig.html)- Config
- A type used to indicate which kind of items we have to generate.
- [Rust](https://docs.rs/struct.RustTarget.html)- Target
- Represents the version of the Rust language to target.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Abi](https://docs.rs/enum.Abi.html)
- A valid rust ABI.
- [Alias](https://docs.rs/enum.AliasVariation.html)- Variation
- Enum for how aliases should be translated.
- [Bindgen](https://docs.rs/enum.BindgenError.html)- Error
- Error type for rust-bindgen.
- [Enum](https://docs.rs/enum.EnumVariation.html)- Variation
- A helper type that represents different enum variations.
- [Field](https://docs.rs/enum.FieldVisibilityKind.html)- Visibility - Kind
- What kind of visibility modifier should be used for a struct or field?
- [Formatter](https://docs.rs/enum.Formatter.html)
- Formatting tools that can be used to format the bindings
- [Macro](https://docs.rs/enum.MacroTypeVariation.html)- Type - Variation
- Enum for the default type of macro constants.
- [NonCopy](https://docs.rs/enum.NonCopyUnionStyle.html)- Union - Style
- Enum for how non-`Copy``union`s should be translated.
- [Rust](https://docs.rs/enum.RustEdition.html)- Edition
- Represents Rust Edition for the generated bindings

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [Cargo](https://docs.rs/constant.CargoCallbacks.html)- Callbacks - Deprecated
- Create a new `CargoCallbacks`value with`CargoCallbacks::rerun_on_header_files`
- [DEFAULT_](https://docs.rs/constant.DEFAULT_ANON_FIELDS_PREFIX.html)- ANON_ - FIELDS_ - PREFIX
- Default prefix for the anon fields.
- [LATEST_](https://docs.rs/constant.LATEST_STABLE_RUST.html)- STABLE_ - RUST
- Latest stable release of Rust that is supported by bindgen

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [builder](https://docs.rs/fn.builder.html)
- Construct a new `Builder`
- [clang_](https://docs.rs/fn.clang_version.html)- version
- Get the major and the minor semver numbers of Clang’s version

# bindgen - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bindgen/0.72.1/bindgen/index.html

## Expand description

Generate Rust bindings for C and C++ libraries.

Provide a C/C++ header file, receive Rust FFI code to call into C/C++ functions and use types defined in the header.

See the [ Builder](https://docs.rs/struct.Builder.html) struct for usage.

See the [Users Guide](https://rust-lang.github.io/rust-bindgen/) for
additional documentation.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [callbacks](https://docs.rs/callbacks/index.html)
- A public API for more fine-grained customization of bindgen behavior.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Bindings](https://docs.rs/struct.Bindings.html)
- Generated Rust bindings.
- [Builder](https://docs.rs/struct.Builder.html)
- Configure and generate Rust bindings for a C/C++ header.
- [Cargo](https://docs.rs/struct.CargoCallbacks.html)- Callbacks
- A `ParseCallbacks`implementation that will act on file includes by echoing a rerun-if-changed line and on env variable usage by echoing a rerun-if-env-changed line
- [Clang](https://docs.rs/struct.ClangVersion.html)- Version
- Extracted Clang version data
- [Codegen](https://docs.rs/struct.CodegenConfig.html)- Config
- A type used to indicate which kind of items we have to generate.
- [Rust](https://docs.rs/struct.RustTarget.html)- Target
- Represents the version of the Rust language to target.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Abi](https://docs.rs/enum.Abi.html)
- A valid rust ABI.
- [Alias](https://docs.rs/enum.AliasVariation.html)- Variation
- Enum for how aliases should be translated.
- [Bindgen](https://docs.rs/enum.BindgenError.html)- Error
- Error type for rust-bindgen.
- [Enum](https://docs.rs/enum.EnumVariation.html)- Variation
- A helper type that represents different enum variations.
- [Field](https://docs.rs/enum.FieldVisibilityKind.html)- Visibility - Kind
- What kind of visibility modifier should be used for a struct or field?
- [Formatter](https://docs.rs/enum.Formatter.html)
- Formatting tools that can be used to format the bindings
- [Macro](https://docs.rs/enum.MacroTypeVariation.html)- Type - Variation
- Enum for the default type of macro constants.
- [NonCopy](https://docs.rs/enum.NonCopyUnionStyle.html)- Union - Style
- Enum for how non-`Copy``union`s should be translated.
- [Rust](https://docs.rs/enum.RustEdition.html)- Edition
- Represents Rust Edition for the generated bindings

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [Cargo](https://docs.rs/constant.CargoCallbacks.html)- Callbacks - Deprecated
- Create a new `CargoCallbacks`value with`CargoCallbacks::rerun_on_header_files`
- [DEFAULT_](https://docs.rs/constant.DEFAULT_ANON_FIELDS_PREFIX.html)- ANON_ - FIELDS_ - PREFIX
- Default prefix for the anon fields.
- [LATEST_](https://docs.rs/constant.LATEST_STABLE_RUST.html)- STABLE_ - RUST
- Latest stable release of Rust that is supported by bindgen

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [builder](https://docs.rs/fn.builder.html)
- Construct a new `Builder`
- [clang_](https://docs.rs/fn.clang_version.html)- version
- Get the major and the minor semver numbers of Clang’s version

[88](#88)fn file_is_cpp(name_file: &str) -> bool {
[89](#89)    Path::new(name_file).extension().is_some_and(|ext| {
[90](#90)        ext.eq_ignore_ascii_case("hpp") ||
[91](#91)            ext.eq_ignore_ascii_case("hxx") ||
[92](#92)            ext.eq_ignore_ascii_case("hh") ||
[93](#93)            ext.eq_ignore_ascii_case("h++")
[94](#94)    })
[95](#95)}
[96](#96)
[97](#97)fn args_are_cpp(clang_args: &[Box<str>]) -> bool {
[98](#98)    for w in clang_args.windows(2) {
[99](#99)        if w[0].as_ref() == "-xc++" || w[1].as_ref() == "-xc++" {
[100](#100)            return true;
[101](#101)        }
[102](#102)        if w[0].as_ref() == "-x" && w[1].as_ref() == "c++" {
[103](#103)            return true;
[104](#104)        }
[105](#105)        if w[0].as_ref() == "-include" && file_is_cpp(w[1].as_ref()) {
[106](#106)            return true;
[107](#107)        }
[108](#108)    }
[109](#109)    false
[110](#110)}

[319](#319)impl Builder {
[320](#320)    pub fn generate(mut self) -> Result<Bindings, BindgenError> {
[322](#322)        self.options.rust_features = match self.options.rust_edition {
[324](#324)            Some(edition) => {
[325](#325)                if !edition.is_available(self.options.rust_target) {
[326](#326)                    return Err(BindgenError::UnsupportedEdition(
[327](#327)                        edition,
[328](#328)                        self.options.rust_target,
[329](#329)                    ));
[330](#330)                }
[331](#331)                RustFeatures::new(self.options.rust_target, edition)
[332](#332)            }
[333](#333)            None => {
[334](#334)                RustFeatures::new_with_latest_edition(self.options.rust_target)
[335](#335)            }
[336](#336)        };
[337](#337)
[338](#338)        self.options.clang_args.extend(
[340](#340)            get_extra_clang_args(&self.options.parse_callbacks)
[341](#341)                .into_iter()
[342](#342)                .map(String::into_boxed_str),
[343](#343)        );
[344](#344)
[345](#345)        for header in &self.options.input_headers {
[346](#346)            self.options
[347](#347)                .for_each_callback(|cb| cb.header_file(header.as_ref()));
[348](#348)        }
[349](#349)
[350](#350)        self.options.fallback_clang_args = self
[352](#352)            .options
[353](#353)            .clang_args
[354](#354)            .iter()
[355](#355)            .filter(|arg| {
[356](#356)                !arg.starts_with("-MMD") &&
[357](#357)                    !arg.starts_with("-MD") &&
[358](#358)                    !arg.starts_with("--write-user-dependencies") &&
[359](#359)                    !arg.starts_with("--user-dependencies")
[360](#360)            })
[361](#361)            .cloned()
[362](#362)            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
[363](#363)        self.options.clang_args.extend(
[364](#364)            self.options.input_headers
[365](#365)                [..self.options.input_headers.len().saturating_sub(1)]
[366](#366)                .iter()
[367](#367)                .flat_map(|header| ["-include".into(), header.clone()]),
[368](#368)        );
[369](#369)
[370](#370)        let input_unsaved_files =
[371](#371)            std::mem::take(&mut self.options.input_header_contents)
[372](#372)                .into_iter()
[373](#373)                .map(|(name, contents)| {
[374](#374)                    clang::UnsavedFile::new(name.as_ref(), contents.as_ref())
[375](#375)                })
[376](#376)                .collect::<Vec<_>>();
[377](#377)
[378](#378)        Bindings::generate(self.options, &input_unsaved_files)
[379](#379)    }
[380](#380)
[381](#381)    pub fn dump_preprocessed_input(&self) -> io::Result<()> {
[387](#387)        let clang =
[388](#388)            clang_sys::support::Clang::find(None, &[]).ok_or_else(|| {
[389](#389)                io::Error::new(
[390](#390)                    io::ErrorKind::Other,
[391](#391)                    "Cannot find clang executable",
[392](#392)                )
[393](#393)            })?;
[394](#394)
[395](#395)        let mut wrapper_contents = String::new();
[398](#398)
[399](#399)        let mut is_cpp = args_are_cpp(&self.options.clang_args);
[401](#401)
[402](#402)        for header in &self.options.input_headers {
[404](#404)            is_cpp |= file_is_cpp(header);
[405](#405)
[406](#406)            wrapper_contents.push_str("#include \"");
[407](#407)            wrapper_contents.push_str(header);
[408](#408)            wrapper_contents.push_str("\"\n");
[409](#409)        }
[410](#410)
[411](#411)        for (name, contents) in &self.options.input_header_contents {
[414](#414)            is_cpp |= file_is_cpp(name);
[415](#415)
[416](#416)            wrapper_contents.push_str("#line 0 \"");
[417](#417)            wrapper_contents.push_str(name);
[418](#418)            wrapper_contents.push_str("\"\n");
[419](#419)            wrapper_contents.push_str(contents);
[420](#420)        }
[421](#421)
[422](#422)        let wrapper_path = PathBuf::from(if is_cpp {
[423](#423)            "__bindgen.cpp"
[424](#424)        } else {
[425](#425)            "__bindgen.c"
[426](#426)        });
[427](#427)
[428](#428)        {
[429](#429)            let mut wrapper_file = File::create(&wrapper_path)?;
[430](#430)            wrapper_file.write_all(wrapper_contents.as_bytes())?;
[431](#431)        }
[432](#432)
[433](#433)        let mut cmd = Command::new(clang.path);
[434](#434)        cmd.arg("-save-temps")
[435](#435)            .arg("-E")
[436](#436)            .arg("-C")
[437](#437)            .arg("-c")
[438](#438)            .arg(&wrapper_path)
[439](#439)            .stdout(Stdio::piped());
[440](#440)
[441](#441)        for a in &self.options.clang_args {
[442](#442)            cmd.arg(a.as_ref());
[443](#443)        }
[444](#444)
[445](#445)        for a in get_extra_clang_args(&self.options.parse_callbacks) {
[446](#446)            cmd.arg(a);
[447](#447)        }
[448](#448)
[449](#449)        let mut child = cmd.spawn()?;
[450](#450)
[451](#451)        let mut preprocessed = child.stdout.take().unwrap();
[452](#452)        let mut file = File::create(if is_cpp {
[453](#453)            "__bindgen.ii"
[454](#454)        } else {
[455](#455)            "__bindgen.i"
[456](#456)        })?;
[457](#457)        io::copy(&mut preprocessed, &mut file)?;
[458](#458)
[459](#459)        if child.wait()?.success() {
[460](#460)            Ok(())
[461](#461)        } else {
[462](#462)            Err(io::Error::new(
[463](#463)                io::ErrorKind::Other,
[464](#464)                "clang exited with non-zero status",
[465](#465)            ))
[466](#466)        }
[467](#467)    }
[468](#468)}

[524](#524)                    "--newtype-enum",
[525](#525)                    "--newtype-global-enum",
[526](#526)                    "--rustified-enum",
[527](#527)                    "--rustified-enum-non-exhaustive",
[528](#528)                    "--constified-enum-module",
[529](#529)                    "--constified-enum",
[530](#530)                    "--type-alias",
[531](#531)                    "--new-type-alias",
[532](#532)                    "--new-type-alias-deref",
[533](#533)                    "--bindgen-wrapper-union",
[534](#534)                    "--manually-drop-union",
[535](#535)                    "--no-partialeq",
[536](#536)                    "--no-copy",
[537](#537)                    "--no-debug",
[538](#538)                    "--no-default",
[539](#539)                    "--no-hash",
[540](#540)                    "--must-use",
[541](#541)                ])
[542](#542)                .chain((0..self.abi_overrides.len()).map(|_| "--override-abi"))
[543](#543)                .map(Some)
[544](#544)                .collect()
[545](#545)            } else {
[546](#546)                vec![None; sets_len]
[547](#547)            };
[548](#548)
[549](#549)            for (regex_set, name) in
[550](#550)                self.abi_overrides.values_mut().chain(regex_sets).zip(names)
[551](#551)            {
[552](#552)                regex_set.build_with_diagnostics(record_matches, name);
[553](#553)            }
[554](#554)        }
[555](#555)        #[cfg(not(feature = "experimental"))]
[556](#556)        for regex_set in self.abi_overrides.values_mut().chain(regex_sets) {
[557](#557)            regex_set.build(record_matches);
[558](#558)        }
[559](#559)    }
[560](#560)
[561](#561)    pub fn set_rust_target(&mut self, rust_target: RustTarget) {
[563](#563)        self.rust_target = rust_target;
[564](#564)    }
[565](#565)
[566](#566)    pub fn rust_features(&self) -> RustFeatures {
[568](#568)        self.rust_features
[569](#569)    }
[570](#570)
[571](#571)    fn last_callback<T>(
[572](#572)        &self,
[573](#573)        f: impl Fn(&dyn callbacks::ParseCallbacks) -> Option<T>,
[574](#574)    ) -> Option<T> {
[575](#575)        self.parse_callbacks
[576](#576)            .iter()
[577](#577)            .filter_map(|cb| f(cb.as_ref()))
[578](#578)            .next_back()
[579](#579)    }
[580](#580)
[581](#581)    fn all_callbacks<T>(
[582](#582)        &self,
[583](#583)        f: impl Fn(&dyn callbacks::ParseCallbacks) -> Vec<T>,
[584](#584)    ) -> Vec<T> {
[585](#585)        self.parse_callbacks
[586](#586)            .iter()
[587](#587)            .flat_map(|cb| f(cb.as_ref()))
[588](#588)            .collect()
[589](#589)    }
[590](#590)
[591](#591)    fn for_each_callback(&self, f: impl Fn(&dyn callbacks::ParseCallbacks)) {
[592](#592)        self.parse_callbacks.iter().for_each(|cb| f(cb.as_ref()));
[593](#593)    }
[594](#594)
[595](#595)    fn process_comment(&self, comment: &str) -> String {
[596](#596)        let comment = comment::preprocess(comment);
[597](#597)        self.last_callback(|cb| cb.process_comment(&comment))
[598](#598)            .unwrap_or(comment)
[599](#599)    }

[627](#627)#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
[629](#629)#[non_exhaustive]
[630](#630)pub enum BindgenError {
[631](#631)    FolderAsHeader(PathBuf),
[633](#633)    InsufficientPermissions(PathBuf),
[635](#635)    NotExist(PathBuf),
[637](#637)    ClangDiagnostic(String),
[639](#639)    Codegen(CodegenError),
[641](#641)    UnsupportedEdition(RustEdition, RustTarget),
[643](#643)}
[644](#644)
[645](#645)impl std::fmt::Display for BindgenError {
[646](#646)    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
[647](#647)        match self {
[648](#648)            BindgenError::FolderAsHeader(h) => {
[649](#649)                write!(f, "'{}' is a folder", h.display())
[650](#650)            }
[651](#651)            BindgenError::InsufficientPermissions(h) => {
[652](#652)                write!(f, "insufficient permissions to read '{}'", h.display())
[653](#653)            }
[654](#654)            BindgenError::NotExist(h) => {
[655](#655)                write!(f, "header '{}' does not exist.", h.display())
[656](#656)            }
[657](#657)            BindgenError::ClangDiagnostic(message) => {
[658](#658)                write!(f, "clang diagnosed error: {message}")
[659](#659)            }
[660](#660)            BindgenError::Codegen(err) => {
[661](#661)                write!(f, "codegen error: {err}")
[662](#662)            }
[663](#663)            BindgenError::UnsupportedEdition(edition, target) => {
[664](#664)                write!(f, "edition {edition} is not available on Rust {target}")
[665](#665)            }
[666](#666)        }
[667](#667)    }
[668](#668)}
